# Jhāna Saṁyutta (SN 53)

**ID:** SN 53
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Jhāna Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul8.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 53) is the fifty-third collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the *Mahāvagga* (Part V) [Norman 1983; Bodhi 2003]. It comprises 54 short discourses dedicated to absorption meditation (*jhāna*). Bhikkhu Bodhi observes that while the homonymous thirty-fourth saṁyutta (SN 34) focuses on the dyadic permutations of meditative skills and the process of meditation, SN 53 represents the collection explicitly treating the four *jhānas* as meditative attainments [Bodhi 2003].

Structurally, the collection is heavily abbreviated in manuscripts and printed editions, consisting essentially of the application of standard repetition series—such as the *Gaṅgā-peyyāla*, *Appamāda-*, *Balakaraṇīya-*, *Esanā-*, and *Ogha-vaggas*—to the formula for the four absorptions [Gethin 2001]. Consequently, several sections consist merely of mnemonic *uddāna* verses accompanied by editorial instructions to expand the text in full following the pattern of the *Magga Saṁyutta* (*yathā Maggasamyuttaṁ evaṁ Jhānasamyuttaṁ vitthāretabbaṁ*) [Norman 1983; Gethin 2001]. Regarding its doctrinal message, the text employs the simile of the river Ganges slanting, sloping, and inclining toward the east to demonstrate that one who cultivates the four absorptions inevitably inclines toward Nibbāna [Polak 2011]. Furthermore, it asserts that cultivating the four *jhānas* brings about direct knowledge and the destruction of the three taints (*āsava*, SN 53.37) and fetters [Polak 2011].

Because of its formulaic structure, DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse (710 matching passages across 68 texts), most notably with other *Mahāvagga* collections that share the same repetition matrices, such as the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), *Indriya Saṁyutta* (SN 48), *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), *Bala Saṁyutta* (SN 50), and *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47), alongside parts of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* and the Abhidhamma *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12) [DharmaNexus]. Bodhi notes that a counterpart *Jhānasamyutta* occurs among a series of small chapters at the end of the *Maggavagga* section of the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* [Bodhi 2003]. DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of SN 53 with the Sanskrit *Dharmaskandha* and *Saṅgītisūtra*, as well as Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* discourses (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
